name: Belgian Congo
alt: Ruanda-Urundi (mandate and trust territory administered with it)

predecessors.name: Congo Free State
predecessors.text: the whole Congo plus the Lado Enclave, as the Congo Free State dossier hands it over

capitals.name: Usumbura (Bujumbura), seat of the Ruanda-Urundi administration

ledger.x: 1910: the Lado Enclave passes to the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan.
1916: the Belgians take Kigoma and Ujiji.
1916: Belgian troops hold Kigali and Ruanda.
1921: Belgium hands the Kigoma district to Britain.
1922: the occupation of Ruanda-Urundi becomes a mandate.
1922: the League of Nations gives Ruanda-Urundi to Belgium.
1923: the capital moves from Boma to Leopoldville (infobox 'Boma (1908-1923)', 'Leopoldville (1923-1960)').
30 June 1960: the Belgian Congo is independent.
1 July 1962: Urundi becomes independent as Burundi.
1 July 1962: the Belgian administration ends with the independence of Rwanda and Burundi; the land passes to those two states (identity.successors).

wars.name: East African campaign (World War I)
wars.outcome: Allied victory: 'German East Africa partitioned by Britain, Belgium and Portugal'; Belgium obtains Ruanda-Urundi as a B-class mandate (20 July 1922) and cedes the Kigoma district to Britain (22 March 1921).

wars.name: Belgian Congo in the East African campaign (World War II)
wars.outcome: Congolese forces fought the Italians in Italian East Africa in 1940-1941; the Italians surrendered on 3 July 1941.

certainty.note: Colonial frontiers: the Lado Enclave page gives its line as 'the Congo-Nile watershed, the 25th meridian east, the 10th parallel north, and the Nile thalweg'; no page opened itemises the Congo's other treaty lines.
Ruanda-Urundi and Kigoma are military occupation lines, not treaty borders.
The mandate (20 July 1922) and trust-territory (13 December 1946) boundaries and the colonial frontier; no page opened itemises the individual treaty lines.
